## Features

- **MX Creative Keypad support.** With [mx-keypad](https://github.com/hawkish/mx-keypad)'s agent (`mx-keypad run`, v0.7.2 or later) running, the sidebar adds an **agents** page to the keypad over the agent's socket, next to your own mx-keypad pages. The keypad's nine keys cover slots 1–9, so agents beyond the Keychron's four still get a key, and the first four light up on both devices. Each key shows the agent's status colour and blinks like the Keychron, but the icon stays up through the dim half of the blink. Press a key to jump to that agent's pane. tmux-legion never opens the device itself, so it needs no Accessibility or Input Monitoring grant, and closing the sidebar or putting the Mac to sleep takes its pages away again.

- **Agent icons by model.** A key's icon follows the agent's model family rather than the CLI that launched it, so a Claude session shows the Claude icon in Claude Code, opencode, or Copilot CLI alike. The `claude`, `codex`, and `copilot` icons are mx-keypad built-ins. To override them, point `@legion_keypad_icons` at a folder of `<name>.png`, `.svg`, or `.jpg` files.

- **Your own keypad pages.** Put pages in `~/.config/tmux-legion/keypad.json`, in mx-keypad's config format, and the keypad shows them ahead of the agents page while the sidebar is open. mx-keypad's agent performs their actions, so shortcuts, text, media keys, hold, switch, and sequences all work. Edits apply within a second, and a file that doesn't parse leaves the last good pages up.

- **opencode detection.** tmux-legion reads opencode's screen to tell working from blocked (a permission prompt), and picks up its model from the status line.

- **Slots stay consecutive.** Agents are numbered 1, 2, 3… in the order the sidebar lists them, recomputed every reconcile, so closing an agent no longer leaves a permanent gap on the keys.

`@legion_keypad off` disables the keypad backend on a machine that has one.

## Install

### Nix flake

```nix
# Pin to a release tag (recommended); drop the ref to track the default branch.
inputs.tmux-legion.url = "github:hawkish/tmux-legion/v0.8.0";
```

### Manual and TPM-style

```bash
git clone https://github.com/hawkish/tmux-legion ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-legion
cd ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-legion && cargo build --release
echo 'run-shell ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-legion/tmux-legion.tmux' >> ~/.tmux.conf
```

Upgrading needs a tmux config reload, not just a rebuild — see [After upgrading](https://github.com/hawkish/tmux-legion#after-upgrading). The [README](https://github.com/hawkish/tmux-legion#install) covers Claude Code hooks, the agent skill, and the pi extension.
